frameworks.name: Creative-Volume Targeting Framework
frameworks.definition: A market-selection strategy for service delivery businesses that prioritizes high-volume customer needs (50-100+ units per month) over premium-quality lower-volume offerings, targeting buyers already spending $100k+ monthly in the category.

frameworks.name: Full-Service Creative Agency Model
frameworks.definition: A value proposition where the agency handles creative production, fulfillment, and media buying as a unified service, with media buying as the simplest layer and qualified buyer criteria (1+ year profitable advertising, $1M+ annual ad spend) as the gate.

claims.text: The underlying value delivery mechanism in creative services is solving customer operational burden (managing creative talent, filming, scripting, hiring models) rather than the production technology itself—whether the output is made with AI or traditional methods is immaterial to the customer.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Marketing agency or brand services context
claims.mechanism: Customers prioritize time/headache relief over methodology; the technology is a cost-edge, not a selling point.
bounded_by: Does not apply when customers specifically demand a particular technology or methodology
Does not apply in low-volume, bespoke creative contexts

claims.text: For AI-based services entering legacy-dominated markets, hide the AI component as a cost advantage and sell the outcome (lower cost, faster delivery, higher volume capacity) rather than leading with the technology, because legacy practitioners are risk-averse and narratively skeptical of AI regardless of quality parity.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Incumbent customer relationships or legacy industry context
Technology is perceived as threatening to existing workflows
claims.mechanism: Risk aversion and narrative negativity suppress willingness to try new methods; hiding implementation preserves quality perception while capturing cost arbitrage.
bounded_by: Does not apply to early-adopter or tech-forward segments
Does not apply when transparency is contractually or legally required

claims.text: A marketing agency selling creative services to high-spend brands should target buyers with minimum annual ad spend of $100,000 and minimum creative asset need of 50-100 pieces monthly, because these segments have proven volume demand and operational budgets to absorb full-service delivery.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Marketing agency or creative production business
Selling to brands with proven ad budgets

numbers.axis: Buyer segmentation by annual ad spend and creative asset demand

anchors.region: $100k+ annual ad spend with 50-100 pieces monthly

bounded_by: Does not apply to enterprise buyers spending $500k+ per ad (different value lever)

claims.text: In creative services, volume and cost efficiency are more important optimization vectors than premium quality per unit, because customers are buying large production runs for performance testing and iteration rather than individual hero assets.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Customers care about testing hypothesis speed (different message variants, creative formats) and iteration velocity, not production perfection per asset; marginal quality improvement yields diminishing ROI vs. volume increase.

anchors.value: Premium quality, low volume (1-5 per cycle)
Adequate quality, high volume (50-200 per month)

bounded_by: Does not apply to hero brand-building campaigns or cinematic content where production quality is the primary differentiator

claims.text: Price anchoring for creative services should reference broadcast commercial pricing ($500,000 per commercial) as the premium anchor to position standard pricing ($50,000) as a value discount, rather than selling AI's cost advantage ($18,000-20,000 production cost) directly.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Selling to brands accustomed to broadcast pricing

numbers.axis: Price anchoring by commercial production type

claims.text: Enterprise-segment creative services should lead with a single stated price (e.g., $400 thousand) and then pocket the margin benefit from lower production costs, rather than disclosing AI as the cost advantage, to preserve perceived value and market positioning.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Enterprise customer segment ($500k+ annual creative budget)

anchors.value: Single price point with undisclosed margin

claims.text: A full-service creative agency that handles creative production and media buying should qualify buyers by three criteria: 1+ year of profitable advertising track record, minimum $1,000,000 annual ad spend, and proven funnel mechanics before onboarding.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Full-service marketing agency or creative + media buying model

numbers.axis: Buyer qualification criteria for full-service engagement

bounded_by: Does not apply to unproven or testing-stage customers
Does not apply to customers with negative unit economics

claims.text: For marketing agencies, media buying is the simplest operational layer in full-service creative delivery; a single media buyer can handle the entire buying process once creative production is solved, making creative asset production the actual bottleneck to scaling.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Full-service marketing agency or creative + media buying model
bounded_by: Assumes media buying is standardized and not customized per account

claims.text: The next generation of traditional marketing agencies will be those that own the full creative production-to-delivery pipeline (creative ideation, asset production, media buying, performance monitoring), rather than sub-contracting or requiring clients to manage creative talent separately.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: High-volume customer base with ongoing creative needs
bounded_by: Does not apply to specialized creative boutiques serving single-project clients

claims.text: When a customer is unsure which creative assets will perform in market, they prioritize volume and iteration velocity (testing many variants) over production quality per unit, making cost per asset and total production capacity the primary competitive levers.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Paid media or performance marketing context
Early-stage funnel or creative testing phase
claims.mechanism: Uncertainty about performance drives hypothesis-testing mindset; volume of tests de-risks learning faster than quality of individual assets.

numbers.axis: Creative asset economics by customer stage

anchors.region: Proven funnel with known winner creatives

bounded_by: Does not apply to brand-building or reputation-sensitive contexts

examples.text: An AI marketing agency founder with 20 years advertising experience launched a service offering AI-generated commercials (Abe Lincoln, Teddy Roosevelt deepfakes) at $25,000 per ad, with two full-time customers acquired via Google search for high-intent queries. The founder had set production cost at $18,000-20,000 per 30-second commercial and a target price of $50,000. Alex Hormozi identified that the founder was operating in the wrong market segment and pricing model—selling premium quality to SMBs rather than volume to mid-market buyers spending $100k+ monthly on ads.

Hormozi cited a company he examined that had built a DIY tool for ad creation but faced adoption resistance and failed to scale. The company pivot from selling a tooling product to selling marketing agency services—offering better ad quality at lower cost than traditional agencies. By positioning themselves as a more-efficient creative production agency rather than a technology vendor, they found traction because customers cared about the outcome (good ads, lower costs) not the implementation (how those ads were made).

practices.text: For AI-based service businesses selling into legacy industries, position the output as the primary value and keep the AI component hidden or downplayed; lead with cost savings and capability (e.g., 'We can make 200 ads a month') rather than method.

Build a marketing agency business model around full-service creative asset production and media buying, not tooling or templates; focus on owning the entire operational pipeline so customers delegate all creative execution to you.

When targeting mid-market and enterprise creative buyers, pre-qualify on annual ad spend ($1M+ minimum), creative asset volume need (50-100+ monthly), and profitable advertising track record (1+ year) before engaging in sales conversations.
